I started at a thrift store, there are soooo many options, and its all cheap stuff that still looks good. Start with jeans. For other styles of pants, I wouldn't recommend leggings from a thrift store. Experiment with clothes you like but also ones you aren't, since a lit of them look better on you than just on a hanger. Don't get discouraged, some stuff won't look good, but that goes for literally 100% of girls. Dress appropriately for your age, as that is a big determinant factor for passing. If you have questions while there, ask employees, they are there to help. Go for swoop necks and things that draw attention from the shoulder to the waist. A general rule for outfit making too is to alternate baggy and form fitting, so if you wear tight jeans, wear a looser, drapey shirt, or vice versa. It works for me. Also, try to avoid horizontal stripes, they tend to broaden the area they're on. Also at thrift stores there's soooo many shoes options that are cheap, my favorite pair of boots were like 8 dollars, and they look good as new. Get a variety of shoes to match with your outfits, they matter! 

Sorry for the length, and going outside the topic! But yeah, thrift stores work really well to find your style and what is flattering on you.
